experiment: Trip 1b (CRC16 microbenchmark) and an SD write-size sweep, both taken from the default benchmark that the T7 session's R press ran. Config: the T7 file, which has no sections= line, so optical, hash and sd ran with hash_mib=8, chunks 32/128/512, UI at 2 Hz.
agree: BENCH hash uihz=2 crc16 agree=OK (4 implementations, identical results)

conclusions: KOS's CRC16 costs 22.7 cycles a byte of CPU here (worker time; the wall-time cyc_b figures of 24/12/9/25 include the UI's 2 Hz share). The table version costs 11.7, slice2 8.8, nibble 24.9 (slower than KOS's, as predicted from instruction counts). All four return identical values.

Applied to the T7 capture (write phase 63.8% of the time), slice2 would save about 87 s of 1605: a 5.7% faster capture. This is a projection from the microbenchmark, and the gain is on the capture, not the 8% it would be on the SD write alone.

SD writes get slightly faster with larger commands: 1088.7 KiB/s at 32 sectors, 1126.9 at 128, 1148.1 at 512 (expand off), so a 4x larger write is worth about 3.5% on the write alone; reads 631.3 / 639.3 / 648.3.

If the entire disc transfer overlapped with the SD write (DMA, Trip 6a, best case) the capture would take about 1166 s instead of 1605: at most 37.6% faster, about 18 minutes with slice2 too. An upper bound, not a prediction.
